 Local Universal FAFSA Challenge opens applications for $10 million in grant funding
 Lisa Giles 10-27-2026 at 09:55:38 AM EDT | Updated 10-27-2026 at 09:55:39 AM EDT Link Copied! LANSING - Michigan school districts and public school academies can begin applying today for the third round of the $10 million Universal FAFSA Challenge.
 The state program provides grant funding to help local schools assist graduating seniors with completing the Free Application for Federal Student Aid.
 The funding supports school districts in adopting a policy that makes FAFSA completion a requirement for high school graduation, while incorporating an opt-out provision for qualifying students. Participating schools use the grants to implement strategies to help students navigate the financial aid process.
 Advertisement Completing the FAFSA is the initial step for students to access federal, state, and institutional financial aid, including grants, scholarships, and work-study programs. In Michigan, FAFSA submission is required to qualify for state aid initiatives such as the Michigan Achievement Scholarship and the Community College Guarantee.
 School districts and public school academies that received funding in previous rounds of the Universal FAFSA Challenge are ineligible to apply for this third round. During the prior round, participating districts received an average of $781.73 per 12th-grade student.
 MiLEAP will host three informational webinars for school districts interested in applying for the grant program. The virtual sessions are scheduled for Nov. 12 at 1 p.m., Nov. 18 at 11 a.m., and Nov. 20 at 3 p.m.
 Applications are due Dec. 1, 2026. Districts and public school academies that participate in this round must adopt their FAFSA completion policy by June 30, 2027.
